draft.title: Three levels of government
card: Federal
the national government, based in Canberra. It handles matters for the whole country, such as defence, immigration and Medicare.
State
the government of a state, such as New South Wales. It handles matters such as public schools, police and hospitals.
Local
a council that serves a town, city or shire. It handles matters such as rubbish collection, local roads and parks.
Each level looks after the matters that suit its size. Citizens deal with all three levels in daily life.
draft.remember: Federal covers the whole nation, state covers a state, and local covers a community.

a.q: Which matter is mainly handled by a local council?
a.why: Rubbish collection serves a local community, so it is a council matter. Police are a state matter, which makes that option tempting, but a council does not run them.
a.clue: Think about what serves one town or suburb.

b.q: Priya lives in Newcastle. Her street has a damaged footpath and her brother needs a place at a public high school. Which levels of government mainly handle each matter, in that order?
b.why: Footpaths and local roads are looked after by the council, and public schools are run by the state government. Federal government is tempting for schools because it is the biggest level, but the card places schools with the state.
b.clue: Footpaths serve a neighbourhood, and schools are a state matter.

problems.detail: The clue gives the answer away. 'Schools are a state matter' states half the answer outright, and 'footpaths serve a neighbourhood' points straight to the council, so a student can answer without knowing the idea.
Two distractors name their own level ('the nation's defence force', 'the state police force'), so a student can rule them out from the wording alone, without knowing which level handles what.
